glossary.definition: Under the DPDP Act, the organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed.
An entity that processes personal data on a fiduciary’s behalf, such as a model vendor.
The person the personal data is about; a parent or guardian for a child.
A registered entity through which people give, manage and withdraw consent under the DPDP Rules.
A fiduciary designated for volume or risk, with extra duties such as annual impact assessments and audits.
RBI’s Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of AI (August 2025), with seven sutras and six pillars.
SEBI’s 2025 rule making intermediaries solely responsible for data, output and compliance when they use AI tools.
A control that stops an AI system’s actions immediately, without a deployment.
A register of every AI use with owner, purpose, model, vendor and risk tier.
An EU AI Act category, such as credit scoring of individuals, with duties on risk management, logs and oversight.
EU AI Act roles: the provider builds or markets a system; the deployer uses it under its authority.
ISO/IEC 42001’s term for the policies, processes and controls that govern AI across an organisation.
Records that each include the hash of the previous one, so any edit or deletion is detectable.
A short, structured statement of why a decision was made, tied to a written rule.
Documentation of a deployed AI system: purpose, data, results by segment, limitations and oversight.
A provider arrangement under which request and response content is not stored after the response is returned, beyond what is needed to serve it.
The risk that many critical services depend on one provider, so a single outage, price change or exit hits all of them at once.
A documented, rehearsed plan to move a service off a vendor: what moves, how it is tested, how data is returned and deleted, and how long it takes.
An event where an AI system’s development or use causes, or nearly causes, harm to people, property, rights or the environment.
Corrective and preventive action: the fix for an incident and the change that stops it recurring.
A legal or contractual deadline, counted from detection, for telling a regulator or affected people.
An open standard for signed Content Credentials that record how a media file was created and edited.
In India’s IT Rules, audio-visual content created or altered by computer to appear real.
A hidden signal in pixels or audio that marks content as generated and survives many edits.

symptomRouter.symptom: Our agent reads customers’ PAN, Aadhaar and bank details
symptomRouter.advice: Map the data flows, mask identifiers, sign processor contracts, and make erasure reach every store.

symptomRouter.symptom: We are a bank, NBFC or broker launching a customer-facing agent
symptomRouter.advice: Board policy, inventory, validation, kill switch, human review for high-impact decisions and customer disclosure.

symptomRouter.symptom: We have clients or users in Europe
symptomRouter.advice: Check scope, classify the tier, identify your role, and plan for 2 Aug 2026 and 2 Dec 2027.

symptomRouter.symptom: Each regulation is becoming a separate project
symptomRouter.advice: Adopt NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001 and map one control library to all of them.

symptomRouter.symptom: A customer disputes a decision the agent made
symptomRouter.advice: Replay the decision from a tamper-evident record with versions, grounds and reason codes.

symptomRouter.symptom: An auditor asks what the system does and where it fails
symptomRouter.advice: A system card with results by segment, limitations and oversight, plus a plain customer summary.

symptomRouter.symptom: Our agent runs on one external provider’s model on a floating alias
symptomRouter.advice: Agree data terms, pin a dated version with evals on change, add a tested fallback and write an exit plan.

symptomRouter.symptom: An AI system caused harm and nobody is sure whether or whom to notify
symptomRouter.advice: Use a written AI-incident definition and severity scale, a register with owners, and notification playbooks with clocks.

symptomRouter.symptom: Your tool makes realistic images, video or voice and must mark them as AI-made
symptomRouter.advice: Add visible labels, signed C2PA metadata and an invisible watermark, and do not let users remove them.
